sanity_expectations: For any fixed C in the sampled range, f_bound should be nondecreasing in L and remain between 0 and 1, approaching near 0 at very low L and a finite ceiling near 1 at high L.

Increasing C should raise the effective high-affinity weight and reduce the effective high-affinity K_d, so at low-to-intermediate L (especially around a few to a few tens of nM) higher-C curves should show larger f_bound than lower-C curves.

Because the effective exponent increases with C, ligand-response curves at high C should be steeper around partial occupancy than at C≈0; this is a checkable context-dependent steepness change, not only a vertical rescaling.

The strongest visible context contrast should occur when L lies between the two affinity scales, roughly around K_d < L < K_d_low, where weight redistribution, affinity shift, and cooperativity modulation all affect the shoulder and midpoint region.

At very low L all curves should cluster near zero, and at very high L all curves should cluster near saturation, so context effects are weakest in those asymptotic regimes even though intermediate-L differences are pronounced.

rationale: Structure check shows a static algebraic relation with no derivatives, integrals, delays, or hidden state, so this is an explicit two-input response surface f_bound(L,C). The declared V/P roles are structurally consistent and, because freedom_change is none, preserved: sample both declared inputs L and C, and fix all remaining symbols as parameters. Chosen parameters keep the model finite and real over the proposed domain and expose the intended mechanisms without collapsing to a recovery limit. K_d=10 and K_d_low=200 give a 20-fold affinity separation, so the two receptor branches are distinguishable over the ligand scan. frac_high_affinity=0.25 leaves both branches active. weight_exchange_amplitude=0.35 with K_context=80 makes context-driven redistribution visible over C from near 0 to well above the half-effect scale, but keeps the effective high-affinity weight in a physical range here (about 0.25 to 0.568). hill_n=1.3 and cooperativity_context_amplitude=0.9 with K_cooperativity_context=150 make the effective exponent increase from about 1.3 at low C toward about 2.08 at high C, yielding observable context-dependent steepness rather than only weight exchange. affinity_context_amplitude=2.0 and K_affinity_context=120 use the supplied admissible hint range and produce a substantial but finite decrease in the effective high-affinity K_d from 10 toward about 3.2 as C rises, giving the intended horizontal threshold shift. The ligand range 0.01 to 1000 spans far below K_d, through both transition regions, and into near saturation; the context range 0 to 1000 spans below and above all three context half-effect constants (80, 120, 150), so the L-by-C contrast is visible. A log grid for L is appropriate for threshold behavior across decades; a linear grid for C resolves the saturable context dependence on its natural concentration scale. Numerical substitution checks at low, mid, and high conditions were finite and real.
